title: Zoox Starts Charging for Robotaxi Rides in Las Vegas
summary: Zoox said on August 5, 2026 that it will begin charging for robotaxi rides in Las Vegas on August 10, the first paid service for its purpose-built autonomous vehicle. Fares combine a base charge with distance and time, plus destination fees for trips such as the airport or events at the Sphere and T-Mobile Arena. The service runs under a two-year NHTSA commercial exemption covering eight federal motor vehicle safety standards and permitting up to 2,500 vehicles — necessary because the Zoox vehicle has no steering wheel or other traditional driver controls. San Francisco and Austin continue on free rides; California requires two further permits before Zoox can charge there. The day before, Zoox unveiled the final production design of the four-seat carriage-style robotaxi, with manufacturing moving to Hayward, California and scaling toward 100 vehicles per week.
whyItMatters: Charging money is the line between a pilot and a business. Zoox is the first company to take a vehicle with no steering wheel — built from scratch as a robot rather than retrofitted from a car — into paid commercial service, and it got there through a federal exemption rather than by conforming to standards written for human drivers. The 2,500-vehicle ceiling and the Hayward line define how far that exemption can scale before the rules themselves have to change.
